answer_text:
We evaluate
\[
I=\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{2t}{e^{\pi t}+1}\,dt.
\]

For \(t>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{e^{\pi t}+1}
=\frac{e^{-\pi t}}{1+e^{-\pi t}}
=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{n-1}e^{-n\pi t}.
\]
Since
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\int_0^\infty 2t e^{-n\pi t}\,dt
=\frac{2}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2}<\infty,
\]
we may integrate term by term. Thus
\[
I
=2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{n-1}\int_0^\infty t e^{-n\pi t}\,dt.
\]

Now
\[
\int_0^\infty t e^{-n\pi t}\,dt=\frac{1}{n^2\pi^2},
\]
so
\[
I=\frac{2}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n^2}.
\]

The alternating sum is
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n^2}
=\left(1-2^{1-2}\right)\zeta(2)
=\frac12\cdot \frac{\pi^2}{6}
=\frac{\pi^2}{12}.
\]

Therefore,
\[
I=\frac{2}{\pi^2}\cdot \frac{\pi^2}{12}
=\frac16.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac16}
\]
